condition: Pulmonary embolism (outpatient, provoked: oestrogen + long-haul flight)
summary: 34-year-old woman on the combined pill, 5 days after a 10-hour flight: left calf swelling for 3 days, now sudden breathlessness and right pleuritic chest pain; HR 112, SpO₂ 93 %. Wells PE 7.5 (likely).

inputs.hpi: Flew back from London 5 days ago (10 hours). Left calf ache and swelling for 3 days. This morning sudden breathlessness and sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. No cough, no haemoptysis. Takes the combined oral contraceptive pill. Attending for a breast lump review. Urine pregnancy test negative today.

exam.general: Breathless at rest, speaking in sentences.
exam.cardiovascular: HR 112 regular, BP 124/78, heart sounds normal.
exam.msk: Left calf 3 cm larger than right, pitting oedema to mid-shin, tender along the deep veins.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pulmonary embolism
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected pulmonary embolism with clinical DVT, Wells PE 7.5 (likely): CTPA now, interim anticoagulation if delayed; stop the combined pill.

mustInclude.note: Interim therapeutic anticoagulation if CTPA is delayed.

mustExclude.note: Wells PE >4 -> CTPA directly; a D-dimer gate or the DVT cut-off (≥2) does not follow NICE NG158.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: forbidden management item present in web.clinicalPrompts: "• ctpa if wells score ≥ 2 and d-dimer positive - exclude pulmonary embolism." (+1 more).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Two-level Wells PE in the hypoxia/tachycardia prompts: >4 -> CTPA (interim anticoagulation if delayed); ≤4 -> D-dimer, or PERC when probability is low.

guideline.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism
guideline.section: Sections 4-6: clinical probability (Wells/Geneva), PERC in low probability, D-dimer only when probability is not high, CTPA; anticoagulation while awaiting results in high/intermediate probability; high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE: UFH, bedside echocardiography if CTPA not immediately feasible, systemic thrombolysis; Section 9 pregnancy: D-dimer/CUS/CTPA or V/Q, LMWH (NOACs not recommended in pregnancy)
guideline.citation: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. Eur Heart J. 2020;41:543-603.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 - Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: 1.1 DVT: two-level Wells; likely -> proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation if delayed); 1.1 PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) -> CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely -> D-dimer; PERC when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG158. London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: Base PE case for this cluster, in an outpatient clinic (the existing pe-postop-day5 is a ward case). Wells PE: clinical DVT 3 + PE most likely 3 + HR >100 1.5 = 7.5. PERC does not apply (HR, SpO₂, oestrogen).
